texts: The incorrect statement is that systolic murmurs are present in 90 percent of infants with TGA: D.
With an intact septum there is often no murmur at all, and a murmur appears mainly with a VSD or outflow obstruction, sometimes growing louder over time.

Cyanosis is the rule: TGA is the most common cyanotic lesion presenting in the newborn, nearly all infants with an intact septum are blue, and more than 90 percent are recognized within the first day.
In the picture, most of the ten blue newborns are silent and only a few whoosh.
